# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1071
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1071
- **Title**: gh-1065 [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1065` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +924
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:30:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T21:32:00Z

## PR Description

Closes #1065
### Root Cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` and each event started its own run — one human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM `workflow_dispatch` path only; the GitHub-event path bypassed it (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs, owner hand-cancelling duplicates). The per-issue `concurrency:` group only serialized the duplicates into queued no-op burns — it never dropped them.

### Fix

- `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (new): the unit-tested pure decision, gh-1028 parity — same issue + same leg (title-parsed; unknown leg wildcards on either side, known legs must be equal), in-flight (active states, 6h stale-zombie bound) or freshly-completed `success` (10-min freshness window — burst duplicates reach the probe only after the concurrency group releases the first run) ⇒ skip. Strict run_number tie-break: only an OLDER run suppresses, so exactly one survivor per same-second burst. Fail-open on missing/garbled run data (AC3).
- `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`: new `dedup` probe job (per-status `gh api` fan-out, smAgent parity; short-circuits before any API call for `workflow_dispatch`, non-arming lifecycle labels, non-teammate assignees — gh-1029 no-burn parity; catch-all probe-error fail-open). The `teammate` call now gates on `needs: dedup.outputs.proceed == 'true'`; dropped duplicates emit a `::warning::` audit line (AC1). Dispatch-path behaviour unchanged.
- `js/unit-tests/test_teammateEventDedup.js` + `run_teammateEventDedup.json` (new), added to `run_all.json`.

### Test Coverage

- `test_teammateEventDedup.js` — 30 tests, incl. AC4 (simulated assigned+labeled burst → exactly one dispatch + one skip-audit entry; three-event gh-1061 shape), AC2 (fresh-success suppression after concurrency release; known different leg never swallowed; 6h zombie parity), AC3 (broken/missing probe data proceeds). **PASS**
- Workflow wiring guard: dedup job, `needs.dedup` gate, fail-open anchors asserted against the YAML. **PASS**
- Transport smoke: embedded probe script executed against a mocked `gh` — duplicate drop, earliest-proceeds tie-break, 5/5-status-degraded fail-open, dispatch preflight all verified.
- Full suite `run_all.json`: **4548 passed, 0 failed** (was 4548-green baseline + 30 new).

### Notes

- Freshness window is 10 min by design (documented in the module): long enough for burst event delivery + queue lag, short enough that a later human re-assign is never swallowed. Only `conclusion: success` owns the window — cancelled/failed runs leave the retry path open.
- `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (consumer-repo copy) not touched — its run titles already carry the leg; a follow-up can mirror the gate there if wanted.
- The probe adds one small job per arming event (~seconds: checkout + ≤5 API calls); lifecycle-label events short-circuit with zero API calls.

# gh-1065: [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)

## Description

## Goal — one assignment triggers exactly one teammate run (v1, bug)

**Observed 2026-10-18, IstiN/dmtools-agents:** assigning issues #1040–#1043 started TWO `ai-teammate.yml` runs per issue at 20:11Z (one manually cancelled each); #1061 got three runs across 20:07–20:15. The owner cancels the duplicates by hand.

## Root cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` directly AND the SM tick dispatches the same legs via `workflow_dispatch`. A single human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events, and neither path checks whether a leg for the same issue is already running/queued. gh-1028 dedup covers SM-internal dispatch only; the GitHub-event path bypasses the SM ledger.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — Assigning an issue (with or without a simultaneous label event) yields exactly ONE teammate run per issue per leg; the second trigger within the dedup window is dropped with an audit log line.
- **AC2** — The dedup key and window match the SM-side dispatch dedup (gh-1028) semantics: same issue + same leg + in-flight or freshly-completed run ⇒ skip.
- **AC3** — Event-path dedup is fail-open on probe errors (a broken dedup check must not silently swallow the only trigger).
- **AC4** — Unit test: simulated assigned+labeled double event → one dispatch, one skip-audit entry.

## Non-goals

- Changing which events are allowed to trigger (assigned/labeled stay — the fix is dedup, not removal).

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1071
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1071
- **Title**: gh-1065 [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1065` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +924
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:30:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T21:32:00Z

## PR Description

Closes #1065
### Root Cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` and each event started its own run — one human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM `workflow_dispatch` path only; the GitHub-event path bypassed it (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs, owner hand-cancelling duplicates). The per-issue `concurrency:` group only serialized the duplicates into queued no-op burns — it never dropped them.

### Fix

- `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (new): the unit-tested pure decision, gh-1028 parity — same issue + same leg (title-parsed; unknown leg wildcards on either side, known legs must be equal), in-flight (active states, 6h stale-zombie bound) or freshly-completed `success` (10-min freshness window — burst duplicates reach the probe only after the concurrency group releases the first run) ⇒ skip. Strict run_number tie-break: only an OLDER run suppresses, so exactly one survivor per same-second burst. Fail-open on missing/garbled run data (AC3).
- `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`: new `dedup` probe job (per-status `gh api` fan-out, smAgent parity; short-circuits before any API call for `workflow_dispatch`, non-arming lifecycle labels, non-teammate assignees — gh-1029 no-burn parity; catch-all probe-error fail-open). The `teammate` call now gates on `needs: dedup.outputs.proceed == 'true'`; dropped duplicates emit a `::warning::` audit line (AC1). Dispatch-path behaviour unchanged.
- `js/unit-tests/test_teammateEventDedup.js` + `run_teammateEventDedup.json` (new), added to `run_all.json`.

### Test Coverage

- `test_teammateEventDedup.js` — 30 tests, incl. AC4 (simulated assigned+labeled burst → exactly one dispatch + one skip-audit entry; three-event gh-1061 shape), AC2 (fresh-success suppression after concurrency release; known different leg never swallowed; 6h zombie parity), AC3 (broken/missing probe data proceeds). **PASS**
- Workflow wiring guard: dedup job, `needs.dedup` gate, fail-open anchors asserted against the YAML. **PASS**
- Transport smoke: embedded probe script executed against a mocked `gh` — duplicate drop, earliest-proceeds tie-break, 5/5-status-degraded fail-open, dispatch preflight all verified.
- Full suite `run_all.json`: **4548 passed, 0 failed** (was 4548-green baseline + 30 new).

### Notes

- Freshness window is 10 min by design (documented in the module): long enough for burst event delivery + queue lag, short enough that a later human re-assign is never swallowed. Only `conclusion: success` owns the window — cancelled/failed runs leave the retry path open.
- `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (consumer-repo copy) not touched — its run titles already carry the leg; a follow-up can mirror the gate there if wanted.
- The probe adds one small job per arming event (~seconds: checkout + ≤5 API calls); lifecycle-label events short-circuit with zero API calls.

# gh-1065: [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)

## Description

## Goal — one assignment triggers exactly one teammate run (v1, bug)

**Observed 2026-10-18, IstiN/dmtools-agents:** assigning issues #1040–#1043 started TWO `ai-teammate.yml` runs per issue at 20:11Z (one manually cancelled each); #1061 got three runs across 20:07–20:15. The owner cancels the duplicates by hand.

## Root cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` directly AND the SM tick dispatches the same legs via `workflow_dispatch`. A single human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events, and neither path checks whether a leg for the same issue is already running/queued. gh-1028 dedup covers SM-internal dispatch only; the GitHub-event path bypasses the SM ledger.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — Assigning an issue (with or without a simultaneous label event) yields exactly ONE teammate run per issue per leg; the second trigger within the dedup window is dropped with an audit log line.
- **AC2** — The dedup key and window match the SM-side dispatch dedup (gh-1028) semantics: same issue + same leg + in-flight or freshly-completed run ⇒ skip.
- **AC3** — Event-path dedup is fail-open on probe errors (a broken dedup check must not silently swallow the only trigger).
- **AC4** — Unit test: simulated assigned+labeled double event → one dispatch, one skip-audit entry.

## Non-goals

- Changing which events are allowed to trigger (assigned/labeled stay — the fix is dedup, not removal).

Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,

Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1071
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1071
- **Title**: gh-1065 [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1065` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +924
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:30:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T21:32:00Z

## PR Description

Closes #1065
### Root Cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` and each event started its own run — one human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM `workflow_dispatch` path only; the GitHub-event path bypassed it (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs, owner hand-cancelling duplicates). The per-issue `concurrency:` group only serialized the duplicates into queued no-op burns — it never dropped them.

### Fix

- `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (new): the unit-tested pure decision, gh-1028 parity — same issue + same leg (title-parsed; unknown leg wildcards on either side, known legs must be equal), in-flight (active states, 6h stale-zombie bound) or freshly-completed `success` (10-min freshness window — burst duplicates reach the probe only after the concurrency group releases the first run) ⇒ skip. Strict run_number tie-break: only an OLDER run suppresses, so exactly one survivor per same-second burst. Fail-open on missing/garbled run data (AC3).
- `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`: new `dedup` probe job (per-status `gh api` fan-out, smAgent parity; short-circuits before any API call for `workflow_dispatch`, non-arming lifecycle labels, non-teammate assignees — gh-1029 no-burn parity; catch-all probe-error fail-open). The `teammate` call now gates on `needs: dedup.outputs.proceed == 'true'`; dropped duplicates emit a `::warning::` audit line (AC1). Dispatch-path behaviour unchanged.
- `js/unit-tests/test_teammateEventDedup.js` + `run_teammateEventDedup.json` (new), added to `run_all.json`.

### Test Coverage

- `test_teammateEventDedup.js` — 30 tests, incl. AC4 (simulated assigned+labeled burst → exactly one dispatch + one skip-audit entry; three-event gh-1061 shape), AC2 (fresh-success suppression after concurrency release; known different leg never swallowed; 6h zombie parity), AC3 (broken/missing probe data proceeds). **PASS**
- Workflow wiring guard: dedup job, `needs.dedup` gate, fail-open anchors asserted against the YAML. **PASS**
- Transport smoke: embedded probe script executed against a mocked `gh` — duplicate drop, earliest-proceeds tie-break, 5/5-status-degraded fail-open, dispatch preflight all verified.
- Full suite `run_all.json`: **4548 passed, 0 failed** (was 4548-green baseline + 30 new).

### Notes

- Freshness window is 10 min by design (documented in the module): long enough for burst event delivery + queue lag, short enough that a later human re-assign is never swallowed. Only `conclusion: success` owns the window — cancelled/failed runs leave the retry path open.
- `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (consumer-repo copy) not touched — its run titles already carry the leg; a follow-up can mirror the gate there if wanted.
- The probe adds one small job per arming event (~seconds: checkout + ≤5 API calls); lifecycle-label events short-circuit with zero API calls.

# gh-1065: [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)

## Description

## Goal — one assignment triggers exactly one teammate run (v1, bug)

**Observed 2026-10-18, IstiN/dmtools-agents:** assigning issues #1040–#1043 started TWO `ai-teammate.yml` runs per issue at 20:11Z (one manually cancelled each); #1061 got three runs across 20:07–20:15. The owner cancels the duplicates by hand.

## Root cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` directly AND the SM tick dispatches the same legs via `workflow_dispatch`. A single human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events, and neither path checks whether a leg for the same issue is already running/queued. gh-1028 dedup covers SM-internal dispatch only; the GitHub-event path bypasses the SM ledger.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — Assigning an issue (with or without a simultaneous label event) yields exactly ONE teammate run per issue per leg; the second trigger within the dedup window is dropped with an audit log line.
- **AC2** — The dedup key and window match the SM-side dispatch dedup (gh-1028) semantics: same issue + same leg + in-flight or freshly-completed run ⇒ skip.
- **AC3** — Event-path dedup is fail-open on probe errors (a broken dedup check must not silently swallow the only trigger).
- **AC4** — Unit test: simulated assigned+labeled double event → one dispatch, one skip-audit entry.

## Non-goals

- Changing which events are allowed to trigger (assigned/labeled stay — the fix is dedup, not removal).

diff --git a/.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml b/.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml
index 69f2a638..4b35bdc1 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml
@@ -62,6 +62,132 @@ concurrency:
   cancel-in-progress: false
 
 jobs:
+  # gh-1065 (live 2026-10-18, issues #1040–#1043 / #1061): one human action
+  # (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits MULTIPLE issues events and
+  # each event started its own run — two per issue, three on #1061, the
+  # owner hand-cancelling duplicates. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM
+  # dispatch path only; this job is the missing event-path gate. It probes
+  # the repo's ai-teammate.yml runs (per-status gh api fan-out, smAgent
+  # parity) and lets the `teammate` call fire only when no OLDER run for
+  # the same issue + leg is in flight or freshly completed. Probe errors
+  # FAIL OPEN (AC3): a broken check writes proceed=true so the only trigger
+  # of a burst is never silently swallowed. The decision itself is the
+  # unit-tested pure module js/common/teammateEventDedup.js (AC4) — this
+  # step is transport only. The probe short-circuits BEFORE any API call
+  # for workflow_dispatch (SM-side gh-1028 governs it), non-arming
+  # lifecycle labels (the teammate gate below rejects them — gh-1029 no-burn
+  # parity) and non-teammate assignees.
+  dedup:
+    name: Event-path dedup probe (gh-1065)
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    outputs:
+      proceed: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.proceed }}
+      audit: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.audit }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - id: probe
+        name: Decide whether this event duplicates an in-flight teammate run
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
+          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
+          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
+          LABEL_NAME: ${{ github.event.label.name }}
+          ISSUE_LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
+          ISSUE: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
+          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
+          SELF_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
+          SELF_RUN_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
+          WORKFLOW_FILE: ai-teammate.yml
+          # GITHUB_OUTPUT is provided by the runner — do NOT set it here.
+        run: |
+          node <<'DEDUP_PROBE_EOF'
+          const { execFileSync } = require('child_process');
+          const fs = require('fs');
+          const dedup = require('./js/common/teammateEventDedup.js');
+
+          const env = process.env;
+          const issueLabels = (env.ISSUE_LABELS || '').split(' ').filter(Boolean);
+          const assignees = (env.ASSIGNEES || '').split(' ').filter(Boolean);
+
+          const out = (proceed, audit) => {
+            const line = String(audit).replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
+            fs.appendFileSync(env.GITHUB_OUTPUT || '/dev/null',
+              `proceed=${proceed}\naudit=${line}\n`);
+            console.log((proceed ? '::notice::' : '::warning::') + line);
+          };
+
+          try {
+            // Mirror of the teammate job gate: skip the probe entirely (no
+            // API burn, gh-1029 parity) for everything the gate below would
+            // reject, and for the dispatch path (SM-side dedup governs it).
+            let preflight = null;
+            if (env.EVENT_NAME === 'workflow_dispatch') {
+              preflight = 'dispatch path: governed by the SM-side gh-1028 dedup';
+            } else if (env.ACTION === 'labeled' &&
+                       !dedup.ARMING_LABEL_LEGS.hasOwnProperty(env.LABEL_NAME || '')) {
+              preflight = 'non-arming label: the teammate gate rejects it; no probe spent';
+            } else if (env.ACTION === 'assigned' && assignees.indexOf('ai-teammate') === -1) {
+              preflight = 'not assigned to ai-teammate: the teammate gate rejects it; no probe spent';
+            }
+            if (preflight) {
+              out(true, 'teammate dedup (gh-1065): ' + preflight + '; proceeding');
+              process.exit(0);
+            }
+
+            // Per-status fan-out (smAgent parity): the four active states plus
+            // 'completed' (the freshness window needs recently-settled runs —
+            // burst duplicates reach this probe only after the concurrency
+            // group releases the first run). Each status is best-effort: a
+            // failing status is logged and skipped — if EVERY status failed,
+            // the run list is empty and the decision fails open by design.
+            const statuses = ['queued', 'in_progress', 'waiting', 'pending', 'completed'];
+            let runs = [];
+            let probeErrors = 0;
+            for (const status of statuses) {
+              try {
+                const raw = execFileSync('gh', [
+                  'api', `repos/${env.REPO}/actions/workflows/${env.WORKFLOW_FILE}/runs`,
+                  '-X', 'GET', '-f', `status=${status}`, '-f', 'per_page=50',
+                  '--jq', '.workflow_runs[] | {id, run_number, name, status, conclusion, created_at, updated_at, path}'
+                ], { encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024 });
+                const batch = raw.trim() ? raw.trim().split('\n').filter(Boolean)
+                  .map((l) => { try { return JSON.parse(l); } catch (e) { return null; } })
+                  .filter(Boolean) : [];
+                runs = runs.concat(batch);
+              } catch (e) {
+                probeErrors++;
+                console.log(`::notice::teammate dedup (gh-1065): ${status} probe failed (${(e.message || e).toString().slice(0, 120)}) — status skipped, fail-open`);
+              }
+            }
+
+            const verdict = dedup.decideEventDedup({
+              eventName: env.EVENT_NAME,
+              action: env.ACTION,
+              labelName: env.LABEL_NAME || undefined,
+              issueLabelNames: issueLabels,
+              issue: parseInt(env.ISSUE, 10),
+              workflowFile: env.WORKFLOW_FILE,
+              runs: runs,
+              // The run_number tie-break needs no clock on the self side:
+              // REST always carries run_number for every run.
+              selfRun: {
+                id: parseInt(env.SELF_ID, 10),
+                runNumber: parseInt(env.SELF_RUN_NUMBER, 10)
+              }
+            });
+            const suffix = probeErrors > 0 && verdict.proceed
+              ? ` (${probeErrors}/${statuses.length} probe statuses failed — degraded, fail-open)` : '';
+            out(verdict.proceed, verdict.audit + suffix);
+          } catch (e) {
+            // AC3 fail-open, catch-all: an unexpected probe crash must never
+            // fail the job (that would wedge the dispatch path behind needs:)
+            // and must never swallow the only trigger — proceed with an audit.
+            out(true, 'teammate dedup (gh-1065): probe degraded — fail-open (' +
+              (e && e.message ? e.message : e) + '); proceeding so the only trigger is never swallowed');
+          }
+          DEDUP_PROBE_EOF
+
   teammate:
     # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
     # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
@@ -72,18 +198,24 @@ jobs:
     # 2026-10-18). The gate therefore keys the action: `assigned` requires
     # the ai-teammate assignee; `labeled` proceeds ONLY for the arming
     # labels — lifecycle labels never allocate a runner.
+    #
+    # gh-1065: the call additionally needs the event-path dedup probe
+    # (needs.dedup) — the probe outputs proceed=true unconditionally for
+    # the dispatch path, so workflow_dispatch behaviour is unchanged.
+    needs: dedup
     if: >-
-      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
-      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
-       github.event.action == 'assigned' &&
-       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
-      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
-       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
-       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
-        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
-        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
-        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
-        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
+      needs.dedup.outputs.proceed == 'true' &&
+      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
+       (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
+        github.event.action == 'assigned' &&
+        contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
+       (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
+        github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
+        (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
+         github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
+         github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
+         github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
+         github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved')))
     uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
     with:
       issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
diff --git a/js/common/teammateEventDedup.js b/js/common/teammateEventDedup.js
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..e2cb607a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/js/common/teammateEventDedup.js
@@ -0,0 +1,403 @@
+/**
+ * teammateEventDedup.js — gh-1065 event-path trigger dedup (pure side).
+ *
+ * Live evidence (dmtools-agents 2026-10-18, issues #1040–#1043 / #1061):
+ * ONE human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits MULTIPLE
+ * issues events (`assigned` + one `labeled` per label write), and
+ * .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml triggered one teammate run PER event
+ * — two runs per issue at 20:11Z, three on #1061 across 20:07–20:15,
+ * each duplicate hand-cancelled by the owner. The gh-1028 dedup
+ * (branchLegGuard.js + smAgent.triggerWorkflow) covers the SM-internal
+ * workflow_dispatch path only; the GitHub-event path bypassed that ledger.
+ * The per-issue `concurrency:` group (cancel-in-progress:false) only
+ * SERIALIZES the duplicates into queued no-op burns — it never drops them.
+ *
+ * This module is the missing gate: an issues-event run proceeds only when
+ * NO OTHER ai-teammate run for the SAME issue + leg is in flight (active
+ * status, gh-1028 stale-zombie parity) or freshly completed (a fulfilled
+ * leg owns a short freshness window — burst duplicates of one action land
+ * after the first run because the concurrency group queues them). The key
+ * semantics mirror the SM side (gh-1028): same issue + same leg, where the
+ * run's leg is recovered from its run title (dispatch titles carry the
+ * leg; event-path titles do not) and an unknown leg on either side
+ * wildcards — precision where both legs are known, conservatism for the
+ * burst shapes the titles cannot distinguish.
+ *
+ * Tie-break (AC1, exactly one survivor): only a run that is STRICTLY OLDER
+ * than the probing run suppresses it (run_number order, created_at
+ * fallback). Burst runs are created milliseconds apart in run_number order,
+ * so the earliest always proceeds and every later duplicate of the burst
+ * drops — regardless of which probe executes first.
+ *
+ * FAIL-OPEN (AC3): the transport (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml dedup
+ * job) treats a probe error as "no data" — this module maps a missing/
+ * non-array run list to proceed, so a broken dedup check can never
+ * silently swallow the only trigger.
+ *
+ * Pure functions, no tool globals — the workflow wires the transport
+ * (gh api per-status fan-out, smAgent parity). GraalJS-clean: var + plain
+ * functions, JSON-safe data only.
+ */
+

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1071
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1071
- **Title**: gh-1065 [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1065` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +924
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:30:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T21:32:00Z

## PR Description

Closes #1065
### Root Cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` and each event started its own run — one human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM `workflow_dispatch` path only; the GitHub-event path bypassed it (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs, owner hand-cancelling duplicates). The per-issue `concurrency:` group only serialized the duplicates into queued no-op burns — it never dropped them.

### Fix

- `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (new): the unit-tested pure decision, gh-1028 parity — same issue + same leg (title-parsed; unknown leg wildcards on either side, known legs must be equal), in-flight (active states, 6h stale-zombie bound) or freshly-completed `success` (10-min freshness window — burst duplicates reach the probe only after the concurrency group releases the first run) ⇒ skip. Strict run_number tie-break: only an OLDER run suppresses, so exactly one survivor per same-second burst. Fail-open on missing/garbled run data (AC3).
- `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`: new `dedup` probe job (per-status `gh api` fan-out, smAgent parity; short-circuits before any API call for `workflow_dispatch`, non-arming lifecycle labels, non-teammate assignees — gh-1029 no-burn parity; catch-all probe-error fail-open). The `teammate` call now gates on `needs: dedup.outputs.proceed == 'true'`; dropped duplicates emit a `::warning::` audit line (AC1). Dispatch-path behaviour unchanged.
- `js/unit-tests/test_teammateEventDedup.js` + `run_teammateEventDedup.json` (new), added to `run_all.json`.

### Test Coverage

- `test_teammateEventDedup.js` — 30 tests, incl. AC4 (simulated assigned+labeled burst → exactly one dispatch + one skip-audit entry; three-event gh-1061 shape), AC2 (fresh-success suppression after concurrency release; known different leg never swallowed; 6h zombie parity), AC3 (broken/missing probe data proceeds). **PASS**
- Workflow wiring guard: dedup job, `needs.dedup` gate, fail-open anchors asserted against the YAML. **PASS**
- Transport smoke: embedded probe script executed against a mocked `gh` — duplicate drop, earliest-proceeds tie-break, 5/5-status-degraded fail-open, dispatch preflight all verified.
- Full suite `run_all.json`: **4548 passed, 0 failed** (was 4548-green baseline + 30 new).

### Notes

- Freshness window is 10 min by design (documented in the module): long enough for burst event delivery + queue lag, short enough that a later human re-assign is never swallowed. Only `conclusion: success` owns the window — cancelled/failed runs leave the retry path open.
- `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (consumer-repo copy) not touched — its run titles already carry the leg; a follow-up can mirror the gate there if wanted.
- The probe adds one small job per arming event (~seconds: checkout + ≤5 API calls); lifecycle-label events short-circuit with zero API calls.

# gh-1065: [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)

## Description

## Goal — one assignment triggers exactly one teammate run (v1, bug)

**Observed 2026-10-18, IstiN/dmtools-agents:** assigning issues #1040–#1043 started TWO `ai-teammate.yml` runs per issue at 20:11Z (one manually cancelled each); #1061 got three runs across 20:07–20:15. The owner cancels the duplicates by hand.

## Root cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` directly AND the SM tick dispatches the same legs via `workflow_dispatch`. A single human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events, and neither path checks whether a leg for the same issue is already running/queued. gh-1028 dedup covers SM-internal dispatch only; the GitHub-event path bypasses the SM ledger.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — Assigning an issue (with or without a simultaneous label event) yields exactly ONE teammate run per issue per leg; the second trigger within the dedup window is dropped with an audit log line.
- **AC2** — The dedup key and window match the SM-side dispatch dedup (gh-1028) semantics: same issue + same leg + in-flight or freshly-completed run ⇒ skip.
- **AC3** — Event-path dedup is fail-open on probe errors (a broken dedup check must not silently swallow the only trigger).
- **AC4** — Unit test: simulated assigned+labeled double event → one dispatch, one skip-audit entry.

## Non-goals

- Changing which events are allowed to trigger (assigned/labeled stay — the fix is dedup, not removal).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1071
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1071
- **Title**: gh-1065 [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1065` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +924
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:30:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T21:32:00Z

## PR Description

Closes #1065
### Root Cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` and each event started its own run — one human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM `workflow_dispatch` path only; the GitHub-event path bypassed it (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs, owner hand-cancelling duplicates). The per-issue `concurrency:` group only serialized the duplicates into queued no-op burns — it never dropped them.

### Fix

- `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (new): the unit-tested pure decision, gh-1028 parity — same issue + same leg (title-parsed; unknown leg wildcards on either side, known legs must be equal), in-flight (active states, 6h stale-zombie bound) or freshly-completed `success` (10-min freshness window — burst duplicates reach the probe only after the concurrency group releases the first run) ⇒ skip. Strict run_number tie-break: only an OLDER run suppresses, so exactly one survivor per same-second burst. Fail-open on missing/garbled run data (AC3).
- `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`: new `dedup` probe job (per-status `gh api` fan-out, smAgent parity; short-circuits before any API call for `workflow_dispatch`, non-arming lifecycle labels, non-teammate assignees — gh-1029 no-burn parity; catch-all probe-error fail-open). The `teammate` call now gates on `needs: dedup.outputs.proceed == 'true'`; dropped duplicates emit a `::warning::` audit line (AC1). Dispatch-path behaviour unchanged.
- `js/unit-tests/test_teammateEventDedup.js` + `run_teammateEventDedup.json` (new), added to `run_all.json`.

### Test Coverage

- `test_teammateEventDedup.js` — 30 tests, incl. AC4 (simulated assigned+labeled burst → exactly one dispatch + one skip-audit entry; three-event gh-1061 shape), AC2 (fresh-success suppression after concurrency release; known different leg never swallowed; 6h zombie parity), AC3 (broken/missing probe data proceeds). **PASS**
- Workflow wiring guard: dedup job, `needs.dedup` gate, fail-open anchors asserted against the YAML. **PASS**
- Transport smoke: embedded probe script executed against a mocked `gh` — duplicate drop, earliest-proceeds tie-break, 5/5-status-degraded fail-open, dispatch preflight all verified.
- Full suite `run_all.json`: **4548 passed, 0 failed** (was 4548-green baseline + 30 new).

### Notes

- Freshness window is 10 min by design (documented in the module): long enough for burst event delivery + queue lag, short enough that a later human re-assign is never swallowed. Only `conclusion: success` owns the window — cancelled/failed runs leave the retry path open.
- `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (consumer-repo copy) not touched — its run titles already carry the leg; a follow-up can mirror the gate there if wanted.
- The probe adds one small job per arming event (~seconds: checkout + ≤5 API calls); lifecycle-label events short-circuit with zero API calls.

# gh-1065: [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)

## Description

## Goal — one assignment triggers exactly one teammate run (v1, bug)

**Observed 2026-10-18, IstiN/dmtools-agents:** assigning issues #1040–#1043 started TWO `ai-teammate.yml` runs per issue at 20:11Z (one manually cancelled each); #1061 got three runs across 20:07–20:15. The owner cancels the duplicates by hand.

## Root cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` directly AND the SM tick dispatches the same legs via `workflow_dispatch`. A single human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events, and neither path checks whether a leg for the same issue is already running/queued. gh-1028 dedup covers SM-internal dispatch only; the GitHub-event path bypasses the SM ledger.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — Assigning an issue (with or without a simultaneous label event) yields exactly ONE teammate run per issue per leg; the second trigger within the dedup window is dropped with an audit log line.
- **AC2** — The dedup key and window match the SM-side dispatch dedup (gh-1028) semantics: same issue + same leg + in-flight or freshly-completed run ⇒ skip.
- **AC3** — Event-path dedup is fail-open on probe errors (a broken dedup check must not silently swallow the only trigger).
- **AC4** — Unit test: simulated assigned+labeled double event → one dispatch, one skip-audit entry.

## Non-goals

- Changing which events are allowed to trigger (assigned/labeled stay — the fix is dedup, not removal).

Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Read input context:

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1071
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1071
- **Title**: gh-1065 [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1065` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +924
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:30:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T21:32:00Z

## PR Description

Closes #1065
### Root Cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` and each event started its own run — one human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM `workflow_dispatch` path only; the GitHub-event path bypassed it (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs, owner hand-cancelling duplicates). The per-issue `concurrency:` group only serialized the duplicates into queued no-op burns — it never dropped them.

### Fix

- `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (new): the unit-tested pure decision, gh-1028 parity — same issue + same leg (title-parsed; unknown leg wildcards on either side, known legs must be equal), in-flight (active states, 6h stale-zombie bound) or freshly-completed `success` (10-min freshness window — burst duplicates reach the probe only after the concurrency group releases the first run) ⇒ skip. Strict run_number tie-break: only an OLDER run suppresses, so exactly one survivor per same-second burst. Fail-open on missing/garbled run data (AC3).
- `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`: new `dedup` probe job (per-status `gh api` fan-out, smAgent parity; short-circuits before any API call for `workflow_dispatch`, non-arming lifecycle labels, non-teammate assignees — gh-1029 no-burn parity; catch-all probe-error fail-open). The `teammate` call now gates on `needs: dedup.outputs.proceed == 'true'`; dropped duplicates emit a `::warning::` audit line (AC1). Dispatch-path behaviour unchanged.
- `js/unit-tests/test_teammateEventDedup.js` + `run_teammateEventDedup.json` (new), added to `run_all.json`.

### Test Coverage

- `test_teammateEventDedup.js` — 30 tests, incl. AC4 (simulated assigned+labeled burst → exactly one dispatch + one skip-audit entry; three-event gh-1061 shape), AC2 (fresh-success suppression after concurrency release; known different leg never swallowed; 6h zombie parity), AC3 (broken/missing probe data proceeds). **PASS**
- Workflow wiring guard: dedup job, `needs.dedup` gate, fail-open anchors asserted against the YAML. **PASS**
- Transport smoke: embedded probe script executed against a mocked `gh` — duplicate drop, earliest-proceeds tie-break, 5/5-status-degraded fail-open, dispatch preflight all verified.
- Full suite `run_all.json`: **4548 passed, 0 failed** (was 4548-green baseline + 30 new).

### Notes

- Freshness window is 10 min by design (documented in the module): long enough for burst event delivery + queue lag, short enough that a later human re-assign is never swallowed. Only `conclusion: success` owns the window — cancelled/failed runs leave the retry path open.
- `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (consumer-repo copy) not touched — its run titles already carry the leg; a follow-up can mirror the gate there if wanted.
- The probe adds one small job per arming event (~seconds: checkout + ≤5 API calls); lifecycle-label events short-circuit with zero API calls.

# gh-1065: [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)

## Description

## Goal — one assignment triggers exactly one teammate run (v1, bug)

**Observed 2026-10-18, IstiN/dmtools-agents:** assigning issues #1040–#1043 started TWO `ai-teammate.yml` runs per issue at 20:11Z (one manually cancelled each); #1061 got three runs across 20:07–20:15. The owner cancels the duplicates by hand.

## Root cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` directly AND the SM tick dispatches the same legs via `workflow_dispatch`. A single human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events, and neither path checks whether a leg for the same issue is already running/queued. gh-1028 dedup covers SM-internal dispatch only; the GitHub-event path bypasses the SM ledger.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — Assigning an issue (with or without a simultaneous label event) yields exactly ONE teammate run per issue per leg; the second trigger within the dedup window is dropped with an audit log line.
- **AC2** — The dedup key and window match the SM-side dispatch dedup (gh-1028) semantics: same issue + same leg + in-flight or freshly-completed run ⇒ skip.
- **AC3** — Event-path dedup is fail-open on probe errors (a broken dedup check must not silently swallow the only trigger).
- **AC4** — Unit test: simulated assigned+labeled double event → one dispatch, one skip-audit entry.

## Non-goals

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1071
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1071
- **Title**: gh-1065 [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1065` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +924
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:30:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T21:32:00Z

## PR Description

Closes #1065
### Root Cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` and each event started its own run — one human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM `workflow_dispatch` path only; the GitHub-event path bypassed it (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs, owner hand-cancelling duplicates). The per-issue `concurrency:` group only serialized the duplicates into queued no-op burns — it never dropped them.

### Fix

- `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (new): the unit-tested pure decision, gh-1028 parity — same issue + same leg (title-parsed; unknown leg wildcards on either side, known legs must be equal), in-flight (active states, 6h stale-zombie bound) or freshly-completed `success` (10-min freshness window — burst duplicates reach the probe only after the concurrency group releases the first run) ⇒ skip. Strict run_number tie-break: only an OLDER run suppresses, so exactly one survivor per same-second burst. Fail-open on missing/garbled run data (AC3).
- `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`: new `dedup` probe job (per-status `gh api` fan-out, smAgent parity; short-circuits before any API call for `workflow_dispatch`, non-arming lifecycle labels, non-teammate assignees — gh-1029 no-burn parity; catch-all probe-error fail-open). The `teammate` call now gates on `needs: dedup.outputs.proceed == 'true'`; dropped duplicates emit a `::warning::` audit line (AC1). Dispatch-path behaviour unchanged.
- `js/unit-tests/test_teammateEventDedup.js` + `run_teammateEventDedup.json` (new), added to `run_all.json`.

### Test Coverage

- `test_teammateEventDedup.js` — 30 tests, incl. AC4 (simulated assigned+labeled burst → exactly one dispatch + one skip-audit entry; three-event gh-1061 shape), AC2 (fresh-success suppression after concurrency release; known different leg never swallowed; 6h zombie parity), AC3 (broken/missing probe data proceeds). **PASS**
- Workflow wiring guard: dedup job, `needs.dedup` gate, fail-open anchors asserted against the YAML. **PASS**
- Transport smoke: embedded probe script executed against a mocked `gh` — duplicate drop, earliest-proceeds tie-break, 5/5-status-degraded fail-open, dispatch preflight all verified.
- Full suite `run_all.json`: **4548 passed, 0 failed** (was 4548-green baseline + 30 new).

### Notes

- Freshness window is 10 min by design (documented in the module): long enough for burst event delivery + queue lag, short enough that a later human re-assign is never swallowed. Only `conclusion: success` owns the window — cancelled/failed runs leave the retry path open.
- `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (consumer-repo copy) not touched — its run titles already carry the leg; a follow-up can mirror the gate there if wanted.
- The probe adds one small job per arming event (~seconds: checkout + ≤5 API calls); lifecycle-label events short-circuit with zero API calls.

# gh-1065: [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)

## Description

## Goal — one assignment triggers exactly one teammate run (v1, bug)

**Observed 2026-10-18, IstiN/dmtools-agents:** assigning issues #1040–#1043 started TWO `ai-teammate.yml` runs per issue at 20:11Z (one manually cancelled each); #1061 got three runs across 20:07–20:15. The owner cancels the duplicates by hand.

## Root cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` directly AND the SM tick dispatches the same legs via `workflow_dispatch`. A single human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events, and neither path checks whether a leg for the same issue is already running/queued. gh-1028 dedup covers SM-internal dispatch only; the GitHub-event path bypasses the SM ledger.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — Assigning an issue (with or without a simultaneous label event) yields exactly ONE teammate run per issue per leg; the second trigger within the dedup window is dropped with an audit log line.
- **AC2** — The dedup key and window match the SM-side dispatch dedup (gh-1028) semantics: same issue + same leg + in-flight or freshly-completed run ⇒ skip.
- **AC3** — Event-path dedup is fail-open on probe errors (a broken dedup check must not silently swallow the only trigger).
- **AC4** — Unit test: simulated assigned+labeled double event → one dispatch, one skip-audit entry.

## Non-goals

- Changing which events are allowed to trigger (assigned/labeled stay — the fix is dedup, not removal).

So queued/in_progress/waiting/pending/completed all valid.
3. Important correctness: the concurrency group — `concurrency:` group with `cancel-in-progress: false` means duplicates are queued and only start after the first run finishes. When run 501's dedup probe runs, run 500 has already completed. But the probe asks the API for runs of THIS workflow — run 501 querying sees run 500 completed success → freshness window drop. OK.

But when both runs probe... actually they don't probe concurrently since concurrency serializes. But wait — the dedup job runs BEFORE the concurrency? No — concurrency is workflow-level, applies to the whole workflow run including the dedup job. So run 501's dedup job starts only after run 500 fully completes. Fine.

But there's a subtle issue: **the probing run itself appears in the run list with status in_progress**. When run 500's dedup job probes, its own run (500) is in_progress — but selfId filter excludes it. Good, handled.

So SM dispatch is unaffected. Good.

The module doc says unknown leg on either side wildcards. So a fresh review trigger within 10 min of a dev success gets dropped. That's the documented tradeoff ("conservatism"). The PR notes the 10-min window bounds this. This is by design but arguably a real behavior worth an IMPORTANT note? The docstring explicitly acknowledges: "an SM-dispatched 'dev' leg in flight never swallows a genuinely new 'review' trigger" — but that's for the dispatch title carrying a leg. For event-path titles ('teammate: issues #1040', no leg), a fresh review label within 10 min after the dev run's success IS dropped. This is a design tradeoff, documented in the module ("treating '' as a match-all keeps exactly one run per issue per burst (AC1/AC4)"). I could raise as SUGESTION/IMPORTANT question.

Also: does the run title actually contain the issue? Need to check `run-name:` in ai-teammate.yml. The workflow is `on: issues:` with a reusable workflow call. Workflow-level run-name matters. Let me read the full current workflow file.
