{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `decideEventDedup` cannot pass the `crap` quality gate (CI is red)**

The `crap` check failed on this PR (log fetch was unavailable, but I reproduced the measurement locally with the workflow's exact pinned tool, `IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d` from `.github/workflows/quality.yml:26-27`):

```text
decideEventDedup   js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 27
issueOfRunName     js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 11
legOfRunName       js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 9
isOlderRun         js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 9
```

`quality.yml` sets `CRAP_THRESHOLD: 8` and fails when *a function not in the released baseline exceeds the threshold*. All four functions are new, so none is baselined. Since CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)³ + CC, the best possible value (100% coverage) is CRAP = CC — so `decideEventDedup` scores **≥ 27** no matter how well the 30 tests cover it. The gate cannot go green without refactoring.

Please decompose `decideEventDedup` (e.g. extract the per-run suppressor predicate into a named helper — the six-condition loop body — and split the early-return verdict builders), and simplify `issueOfRunName`/`legOfRunName` (the two regex families could share one anchored-token scanner). Re-run `crap4js --threshold 8 js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` to confirm before pushing.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: runs that never executed the teammate leg own the freshness window — the first GENUINE trigger is silently swallowed**

`isFreshlyCompleted` (and the transport around it) treats any `status: completed` + `conclusion: success` run of this workflow as an owner of the issue+leg key. But run-level success no longer implies the leg ran, because the new `dedup` job **always executes and always succeeds** (its catch-all is fail-open by design):

- A non-arming lifecycle label write (`status:*`, `ai_developed`, … — which the legs themselves write constantly, see the gh-1029 comment in the workflow) creates a run whose `teammate` job is skipped by the gate. The `dedup` job succeeds → **the run concludes `success`**, titled `teammate: issues #1040 ` (same issue anchor, leg `''` → wildcard-compatible).
- Now a human assigns the issue to `ai-teammate (or adds `agent:review`) within 10 minutes of that label write. The probe finds this fresh `success` run, older run_number → `duplicate` → **the first and only real trigger is dropped**, with nothing but a `::warning::` line inside a run that GitHub shows as green.

This breaks AC1 in the dangerous direction (zero runs instead of one), and it contradicts AC3's spirit — a dedup check silently swallowing the only trigger. During active work on an issue (labels being written by legs), event-path triggers are effectively suppressed for 10 minutes after ANY run of this workflow, successful or not.

Suggested directions (either or both):
1. Before a `completed` candidate may suppress, verify it actually executed the leg: `gh api repos/{repo}/actions/runs/{id}/jobs` and require a non-`dedup` job with conclusion `success`. One extra API call only when a candidate exists; keeps the module pure via an injected transport hook.
2. Give the `dedup` job an `if:` mirroring the arming gate (see the runner-burn comment on the workflow) so non-arming events produce zero executed jobs — those runs then conclude `failure` (the gh-676 phantom pattern) and own nothing.

Note the unit suite cannot catch this today: the tests feed synthetic run lists where `conclusion: 'success'` is assumed to mean "the leg ran". A regression test needs the transport-level distinction from option 1, or the zero-job conclusion from option 2.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the unguarded `dedup` job allocates a runner for EVERY label write — gh-1029 no-burn regression**

The `dedup` job has no `if:`, and `on: issues: types: [assigned, labeled]` fires on every label write on every issue — including the lifecycle-label storms the legs themselves generate (`status:*`, `ai_developed`, …). gh-1029 deliberately made those events no-burn: the run's only job was skipped by the gate, zero jobs executed, no runner allocated. This PR keeps the skip but adds a real `ubuntu-latest` runner + checkout + node boot (~30–60 s of runner time) per label write, repo-wide, around the clock.

The preflight correctly avoids *API* calls for non-arming events, but the runner burn remains. Please add an `if:` to the `dedup` job mirroring the `teammate` gate (dispatch OR (assigned AND ai-teammate assignee) OR labeled with an arming label). Behaviour is unchanged for admitted events; rejected events return to true zero-burn.

Side benefit relevant to the freshness-window blocker on `isFreshlyCompleted`: with the `dedup` job skipped, those runs execute zero jobs and conclude `failure` (the gh-676 phantom pattern documented in this same file) — so they stop owning the dedup key entirely.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the wildcard leg + 10-min fresh-success window swallows genuinely sequential human actions**

`legsCompatible` wildcards an unknown leg on either side — correct for the in-flight burst (event-path titles carry no leg, and a bare assign declares none). But the same wildcard is applied to `completed` runs inside the freshness window, where the owner is an event-path run titled `teammate: issues #1040 ` (leg `''`).

Consequence: human assigns the issue at T (leg runs, completes `success` at T+4 min). At T+6 min the same human deliberately adds `agent:review` — a genuinely new request, not a burst duplicate. The probe sees the T+4 `success` run: same issue, leg wildcard-compatible, older run_number → **dropped**. The module docstring claims "a later human re-assign is never swallowed", but that only holds after the 10-minute window; any second, *different-leg* arming action within the window is swallowed.

Please confirm this is intended (the PR notes treat the 10-min bound as covering "burst event delivery + queue lag", i.e. seconds — while a human's next deliberate action often lands minutes later, within the same active session). If not intended, consider scoping the wildcard to in-flight owners only: a wildcard **in-flight** owner is almost certainly the same burst; a `completed` owner with unknown leg suppressing a KNOWN new leg is exactly the sequential-action case. At minimum, the docstring's "never swallowed" claim should be corrected.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: space-joined env lists break label/login names containing spaces**

`ISSUE_LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}` (and `ASSIGNEES` two lines below) are re-split with `.split(' ')` in the probe. GitHub label names may contain spaces (e.g. `status:in progress`), and a label/login token containing a space is silently fractured — `agent:dev` would survive, but any future arming label with a space, or an assignee login, would mismatch. Today this is latent (all five arming labels are space-free), but the parse silently degrades.

Prefer a JSON encoding: `ISSUE_LABELS: ${{ toJson(github.event.issue.labels.*.name) }}` and `JSON.parse(env.ISSUE_LABELS || '[]')` in the probe. Same for assignees.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment5.md"}

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1071
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1071
- **Title**: gh-1065 [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1065` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +1250
- **Deletions**: -26
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:30:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T22:27:38Z

## PR Description

Closes #1065
### Root Cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` and each event started its own run — one human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM `workflow_dispatch` path only; the GitHub-event path bypassed it (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs, owner hand-cancelling duplicates). The per-issue `concurrency:` group only serialized the duplicates into queued no-op burns — it never dropped them.

### Fix

- `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (new): the unit-tested pure decision, gh-1028 parity — same issue + same leg (title-parsed; unknown leg wildcards on either side, known legs must be equal), in-flight (active states, 6h stale-zombie bound) or freshly-completed `success` (10-min freshness window — burst duplicates reach the probe only after the concurrency group releases the first run) ⇒ skip. Strict run_number tie-break: only an OLDER run suppresses, so exactly one survivor per same-second burst. Fail-open on missing/garbled run data (AC3).
- `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`: new `dedup` probe job (per-status `gh api` fan-out, smAgent parity; short-circuits before any API call for `workflow_dispatch`, non-arming lifecycle labels, non-teammate assignees — gh-1029 no-burn parity; catch-all probe-error fail-open). The `teammate` call now gates on `needs: dedup.outputs.proceed == 'true'`; dropped duplicates emit a `::warning::` audit line (AC1). Dispatch-path behaviour unchanged.
- `js/unit-tests/test_teammateEventDedup.js` + `run_teammateEventDedup.json` (new), added to `run_all.json`.

### Test Coverage

- `test_teammateEventDedup.js` — 30 tests, incl. AC4 (simulated assigned+labeled burst → exactly one dispatch + one skip-audit entry; three-event gh-1061 shape), AC2 (fresh-success suppression after concurrency release; known different leg never swallowed; 6h zombie parity), AC3 (broken/missing probe data proceeds). **PASS**
- Workflow wiring guard: dedup job, `needs.dedup` gate, fail-open anchors asserted against the YAML. **PASS**
- Transport smoke: embedded probe script executed against a mocked `gh` — duplicate drop, earliest-proceeds tie-break, 5/5-status-degraded fail-open, dispatch preflight all verified.
- Full suite `run_all.json`: **4548 passed, 0 failed** (was 4548-green baseline + 30 new).

### Notes

- Freshness window is 10 min by design (documented in the module): long enough for burst event delivery + queue lag, short enough that a later human re-assign is never swallowed. Only `conclusion: success` owns the window — cancelled/failed runs leave the retry path open.
- `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (consumer-repo copy) not touched — its run titles already carry the leg; a follow-up can mirror the gate there if wanted.
- The probe adds one small job per arming event (~seconds: checkout + ≤5 API calls); lifecycle-label events short-circuit with zero API calls.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `decideEventDedup` cannot pass the `crap` quality gate (CI is red)**

The `crap` check failed on this PR (log fetch was unavailable, but I reproduced the measurement locally with the workflow's exact pinned tool, `IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d` from `.github/workflows/quality.yml:26-27`):

```text
decideEventDedup   js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 27
issueOfRunName     js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 11
legOfRunName       js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 9
isOlderRun         js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 9
```

`quality.yml` sets `CRAP_THRESHOLD: 8` and fails when *a function not in the released baseline exceeds the threshold*. All four functions are new, so none is baselined. Since CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)³ + CC, the best possible value (100% coverage) is CRAP = CC — so `decideEventDedup` scores **≥ 27** no matter how well the 30 tests cover it. The gate cannot go green without refactoring.

Please decompose `decideEventDedup` (e.g. extract the per-run suppressor predicate into a named helper — the six-condition loop body — and split the early-return verdict builders), and simplify `issueOfRunName`/`legOfRunName` (the two regex families could share one anchored-token scanner). Re-run `crap4js --threshold 8 js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` to confirm before pushing.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: runs that never executed the teammate leg own the freshness window — the first GENUINE trigger is silently swallowed**

`isFreshlyCompleted` (and the transport around it) treats any `status: completed` + `conclusion: success` run of this workflow as an owner of the issue+leg key. But run-level success no longer implies the leg ran, because the new `dedup` job **always executes and always succeeds** (its catch-all is fail-open by design):

- A non-arming lifecycle label write (`status:*`, `ai_developed`, … — which the legs themselves write constantly, see the gh-1029 comment in the workflow) creates a run whose `teammate` job is skipped by the gate. The `dedup` job succeeds → **the run concludes `success`**, titled `teammate: issues #1040 ` (same issue anchor, leg `''` → wildcard-compatible).
- Now a human assigns the issue to `ai-teammate (or adds `agent:review`) within 10 minutes of that label write. The probe finds this fresh `success` run, older run_number → `duplicate` → **the first and only real trigger is dropped**, with nothing but a `::warning::` line inside a run that GitHub shows as green.

This breaks AC1 in the dangerous direction (zero runs instead of one), and it contradicts AC3's spirit — a dedup check silently swallowing the only trigger. During active work on an issue (labels being written by legs), event-path triggers are effectively suppressed for 10 minutes after ANY run of this workflow, successful or not.

Suggested directions (either or both):
1. Before a `completed` candidate may suppress, verify it actually executed the leg: `gh api repos/{repo}/actions/runs/{id}/jobs` and require a non-`dedup` job with conclusion `success`. One extra API call only when a candidate exists; keeps the module pure via an injected transport hook.
2. Give the `dedup` job an `if:` mirroring the arming gate (see the runner-burn comment on the workflow) so non-arming events produce zero executed jobs — those runs then conclude `failure` (the gh-676 phantom pattern) and own nothing.

Note the unit suite cannot catch this today: the tests feed synthetic run lists where `conclusion: 'success'` is assumed to mean "the leg ran". A regression test needs the transport-level distinction from option 1, or the zero-job conclusion from option 2.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the unguarded `dedup` job allocates a runner for EVERY label write — gh-1029 no-burn regression**

The `dedup` job has no `if:`, and `on: issues: types: [assigned, labeled]` fires on every label write on every issue — including the lifecycle-label storms the legs themselves generate (`status:*`, `ai_developed`, …). gh-1029 deliberately made those events no-burn: the run's only job was skipped by the gate, zero jobs executed, no runner allocated. This PR keeps the skip but adds a real `ubuntu-latest` runner + checkout + node boot (~30–60 s of runner time) per label write, repo-wide, around the clock.

The preflight correctly avoids *API* calls for non-arming events, but the runner burn remains. Please add an `if:` to the `dedup` job mirroring the `teammate` gate (dispatch OR (assigned AND ai-teammate assignee) OR labeled with an arming label). Behaviour is unchanged for admitted events; rejected events return to true zero-burn.

Side benefit relevant to the freshness-window blocker on `isFreshlyCompleted`: with the `dedup` job skipped, those runs execute zero jobs and conclude `failure` (the gh-676 phantom pattern documented in this same file) — so they stop owning the dedup key entirely.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the wildcard leg + 10-min fresh-success window swallows genuinely sequential human actions**

`legsCompatible` wildcards an unknown leg on either side — correct for the in-flight burst (event-path titles carry no leg, and a bare assign declares none). But the same wildcard is applied to `completed` runs inside the freshness window, where the owner is an event-path run titled `teammate: issues #1040 ` (leg `''`).

Consequence: human assigns the issue at T (leg runs, completes `success` at T+4 min). At T+6 min the same human deliberately adds `agent:review` — a genuinely new request, not a burst duplicate. The probe sees the T+4 `success` run: same issue, leg wildcard-compatible, older run_number → **dropped**. The module docstring claims "a later human re-assign is never swallowed", but that only holds after the 10-minute window; any second, *different-leg* arming action within the window is swallowed.

Please confirm this is intended (the PR notes treat the 10-min bound as covering "burst event delivery + queue lag", i.e. seconds — while a human's next deliberate action often lands minutes later, within the same active session). If not intended, consider scoping the wildcard to in-flight owners only: a wildcard **in-flight** owner is almost certainly the same burst; a `completed` owner with unknown leg suppressing a KNOWN new leg is exactly the sequential-action case. At minimum, the docstring's "never swallowed" claim should be corrected.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: space-joined env lists break label/login names containing spaces**

`ISSUE_LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}` (and `ASSIGNEES` two lines below) are re-split with `.split(' ')` in the probe. GitHub label names may contain spaces (e.g. `status:in progress`), and a label/login token containing a space is silently fractured — `agent:dev` would survive, but any future arming label with a space, or an assignee login, would mismatch. Today this is latent (all five arming labels are space-free), but the parse silently degrades.

Prefer a JSON encoding: `ISSUE_LABELS: ${{ toJson(github.event.issue.labels.*.name) }}` and `JSON.parse(env.ISSUE_LABELS || '[]')` in the probe. Same for assignees.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: track the template mirror as a follow-up ticket**

The PR notes (correctly) leave `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` untouched — its consumer-repo copies keep the un-deduped event path, so every consumer repo still burns duplicate teammate runs on assign-while-labels-change, and the template's run titles already carry the leg so the pure module would slot in directly. Please file a linked follow-up ticket so this deferred scope doesn't evaporate; a one-line mention in the module header (`DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_FILE` consumers) would also help the next reade…

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

# gh-1065: the title carries the LEG for every path — the dispatch input
# leg directly, and for event-path runs the strongest arming label on the
# issue (rework > review > pr_approved → review > dev). legOfRunName
# (js/common/teammateEventDedup.js) parses the trailing token, so a
# COMPLETED owner stays title-precise: the strict completed-owner leg rule
# (a leg-less completed run never swallows a KNOWN new leg) can only work
# when real leg runs carry their leg in the title.
run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && 'rework') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && 'review') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'pr_approved') && 'review') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:dev') && 'dev') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:develop') && 'dev') || github.event.label.name }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # gh-1065 (live 2026-10-18, issues #1040–#1043 / #1061): one human action
  # (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits MULTIPLE issues events and
  # each event started its own run — two per issue, three on #1061, the
  # owner hand-cancelling duplicates. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM
  # dispatch path only; this job is the missing event-path gate. It probes
  # the repo's ai-teammate.yml runs (per-status gh api fan-out, smAgent
  # parity) and lets the `teammate` call fire only when no OLDER run for
  # the same issue + leg is in flight or freshly completed. Probe errors
  # FAIL OPEN (AC3): a broken check writes proceed=true so the only trigger
  # of a burst is never silently swallowed. The decision itself is the
  # unit-tested pure module js/common/teammateEventDedup.js (AC4) — this
  # step is transport only. The probe short-circuits BEFORE any API call
  # for workflow_dispatch (SM-side gh-1028 governs it), non-arming
  # lifecycle labels and non-teammate assignees.
  dedup:
    name: Event-path dedup probe (gh-1065)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1065 rework (review thread — gh-1029 zero-burn parity): this gate
    # MIRRORS the teammate call gate below. `on:` fires on EVERY label
    # write repo-wide, and an unguarded dedup job would allocate a runner
    # (checkout + node boot) per lifecycle-label storm — the exact burn
    # gh-1029 eliminated. Rejected events now execute ZERO jobs: the run
    # concludes failure (the gh-676 phantom pattern) and — because only
    # conclusion 'success' owns the freshness window — can never suppress
    # a trigger for an issue whose leg never ran.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    outputs:
      proceed: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.proceed }}
      audit: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.audit }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - id: probe
        name: Decide whether this event duplicates an in-flight teammate run
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          LABEL_NAME: ${{ github.event.label.name }}
          ISSUE_LABELS: ${{ toJson(github.event.issue.labels.*.name) }}
          ISSUE: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ toJson(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login) }}
          SELF_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          SELF_RUN_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          WORKFLOW_FILE: ai-teammate.yml
          # GITHUB_OUTPUT is provided by the runner — do NOT set it here.
        run: |
          node <<'DEDUP_PROBE_EOF'
          const { execFileSync } = require('child_process');
          const fs = require('fs');
          const dedup = require('./js/common/teammateEventDedup.js');

          const env = process.env;
          // gh-1065 rework (review thread): label/login names may contain
          // spaces — the lists ride as JSON. Fallback: the legacy
          // space-joined shape still parses (defense in depth).
          const parseEventList = (raw) => {
            try {
              const v = JSON.parse(raw || '[]');
              if (Array.isArray(v)) return v.filter(Boolean);

No — burst means assign+label change. Consider: human assigns (no labels on issue) → run 500 proceeds, executes (factory derives leg somehow — maybe nothing to do), completes success at T+4 with leg-less title. At T+6 min, same human assigns AGAIN (deliberate retry/re-arm — "a second bare assign inside the window is burst noise" per the new doc). The module treats the second bare assign as burst noise and DROPS it. Is that right? A deliberate re-assign within 10 min is plausibly a genuine new request... but this is the documented tradeoff, accepted. Fine.

**Issue B — the both-unknown completed rule vs the AC2 burst**: assign-while-labels-change on an issue that already had NO arming labels... wait, assign-while-labels-change means labels ARE being changed. If the label change includes adding 'bug' (non-arming) and removing... the arming-label-derived title leg depends on the issue's CURRENT arming labels. If the human's action adds `agent:dev`: run 500 (assigned) title carries 'dev'; run 501 (labeled agent:dev) title carries 'dev'; completed strict: both known equal → 501 drops ✓.

If the human's action REMOVES `agent:dev` (unlabels) — no event (trigger is assigned+labeled only... 'unlabeled' not in types). OK.

If the human assigns while a teammate-added lifecycle label changes: run 500 assigned with issue having only lifecycle labels → title leg-less. Run 501 labeled status:whatever → **the dedup job's if: REJECTS it** (non-arming) → run 501 zero jobs → conclusion failure → owns nothing ✓. Good — this is the thread-2/3 fix working together.

**Issue C — title leg derivation race in the burst**: run 500 (assigned) created BEFORE the agent:dev label lands (assign event processed first, label added 200ms later): run 500's title = leg-less (no arming label at run creation). Run 501 (labeled agent:dev): title carries 'dev' (label present by then). Sequence: run 500 proceeds (first), executes dev leg, completes success, leg-less title. Run 501 probes: completed owner leg=' vs event leg='dev' → completedLegsCompatible('dev',') = false → **run 501 PROCEDS** → duplicate dev leg runs twice (serialized by concurrency, but both execute). This re-opens AC1/AC2 for the assign-then-label ordering! The rework's own note says: "Without it [run-name leg carry], scoping the wildcard would have re-opened the AC2 hole: the first burst run's title would be leg-less when the labeled duplicate's probe runs after completion" — they fixed the case where the label is already present at run-500 creation. But the ORDER MATTERS: if the `assigned` event run is created before the label write is visible, its title is leg-less and the labeled duplicate (known leg) proceeds.

How likely is that ordering? GitHub delivers events within ~seconds; run-name is evaluated at run creation from the issue's label list at that moment. The `labeled` event implies the label was added — the issue's labels at that moment include it. For run 500 (created from the assigned event), if GitHub processes assigned first (same-second burst), the label may NOT yet be on the issue → leg-less title. Then the labeled duplicate proceeds. This is exactly the AC4 scenario with the events in the other order. Hmm — but wait: in the AC4 scenario, the FIRST event's run is the one that executes; the second event's run probes AFTER the first completes (concurrency). So the duplicate executes the leg a second time ~minutes later. Violates AC1 (exactly ONE run) — the failure mode is duplicate work (the original bug), not suppression. It's a partial reopen: same-leg burst where the first run's title is leg-less AND the second event is labeled-with-known-leg.

Mitigating factors: with a bare assign (no labels), title leg-less; but the burst observed live (#1040–#1043) was "assign-while-labels-change" — labels changed simultaneously. If the human adds agent:dev AND assigns in one action, whichever event GitHub creates first... the labeled event's run sees the label; the assigned event's run may or may not. Probability ~50% per issue. So this fix reduces duplicates but doesn't eliminate them in this ordering. Is this worth flaging? It's a real residual hole in AC1. The previous review's in-flight wildcard covered it; the completed strict rule re-opens it when the owner completed before the probe. Given the burst's earliest run is what executes, and its title may be leg-less... yes — IMPORTANT finding (correctness gap, re-opens part of AC1). Actually could it be BLOCKING? AC1: "Assigning an issue (with or without a simultaneous label event) yields exactly ONE teammate run per issue per leg". With ~50% ordering, two dev legs run. But it's a re-review; the blocker thread-2 was about suppression (worse). This one causes duplicate burns — the very thing the ticket targets. I rate it IMPORTANT-to-BLOCKING... Let me think about whether there's a cheap fix: the labeled duplicate's probe could also treat a completed leg-less owner as compatible when the event is labeled and the label is now on the issue (i.e., the owner run's title resolution is racy) — e.g., completed rule: both-unknown OR both-known-equal OR (event leg known AND owner completed BEFORE the label landed?) — unknowable. Alternative: the earliest-run tie-break means the labeled run 501 could detect that the leg-less completed owner started BEFORE the label was added — not observable from run metadata. Simpler fix: make `assigned`-event runs not claim the title leg... no.

Actually alternative robust fix: keep strict completed rule, but the labeled event leg derivation could ALSO consider `env.LABEL_NAME` already does. The hole is owner-side (title leg-less). Given the run-name is computed once at creation, you can't fix retroactively. But note: run 501's title carries 'dev'. If instead the module treated "completed owner with unknown leg + same issue + owner is OLDER" as compatible ONLY when the event is `assigned` (both-unknown case handles bare assigns)... that's the current behavior. The labeled-known-leg vs leg-less completed owner proceeds. Hmm.

Practical assessment: this residual duplicates at most ONE extra leg run per burst in the unfavorable ordering, serialized behind the first — exactly the pre-fix behavior for that ordering, not a regression vs main. But the PR claims AC1 fixed. I'll raise as IMPORTANT (question + suggested mitigation: e.g., for a completed leg-less owner, also compare the owner's created_at against... nothing available. Or: the run-name for the assigned event could prefer... nothing. Honestly the cleanest mitigation is the jobs-API verification to check whether the owner run actually executed the same leg — but titles don't record inputs... The factory reusable workflow receives `leg: ''` for event paths and derives internally — not visible. So a full fix is hard; flag as a known residual with a suggested cheap dampener: also suppress when the completed owner is leg-less AND the event is `labeled` with known leg AND the owner's title was created within the same burst window... that's basically re-wildcarding. State it as an open tradeoff question — IMPORTANT).

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `decideEventDedup` cannot pass the `crap` quality gate (CI is red)**

The `crap` check failed on this PR (log fetch was unavailable, but I reproduced the measurement locally with the workflow's exact pinned tool, `IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d` from `.github/workflows/quality.yml:26-27`):

```text
decideEventDedup   js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 27
issueOfRunName     js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 11
legOfRunName       js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 9
isOlderRun         js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 9
```

`quality.yml` sets `CRAP_THRESHOLD: 8` and fails when *a function not in the released baseline exceeds the threshold*. All four functions are new, so none is baselined. Since CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)³ + CC, the best possible value (100% coverage) is CRAP = CC — so `decideEventDedup` scores **≥ 27** no matter how well the 30 tests cover it. The gate cannot go green without refactoring.

Please decompose `decideEventDedup` (e.g. extract the per-run suppressor predicate into a named helper — the six-condition loop body — and split the early-return verdict builders), and simplify `issueOfRunName`/`legOfRunName` (the two regex families could share one anchored-token scanner). Re-run `crap4js --threshold 8 js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` to confirm before pushing.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: runs that never executed the teammate leg own the freshness window — the first GENUINE trigger is silently swallowed**

`isFreshlyCompleted` (and the transport around it) treats any `status: completed` + `conclusion: success` run of this workflow as an owner of the issue+leg key. But run-level success no longer implies the leg ran, because the new `dedup` job **always executes and always succeeds** (its catch-all is fail-open by design):

- A non-arming lifecycle label write (`status:*`, `ai_developed`, … — which the legs themselves write constantly, see the gh-1029 comment in the workflow) creates a run whose `teammate` job is skipped by the gate. The `dedup` job succeeds → **the run concludes `success`**, titled `teammate: issues #1040 ` (same issue anchor, leg `''` → wildcard-compatible).
- Now a human assigns the issue to `ai-teammate (or adds `agent:review`) within 10 minutes of that label write. The probe finds this fresh `success` run, older run_number → `duplicate` → **the first and only real trigger is dropped**, with nothing but a `::warning::` line inside a run that GitHub shows as green.

This breaks AC1 in the dangerous direction (zero runs instead of one), and it contradicts AC3's spirit — a dedup check silently swallowing the only trigger. During active work on an issue (labels being written by legs), event-path triggers are effectively suppressed for 10 minutes after ANY run of this workflow, successful or not.

Suggested directions (either or both):
1. Before a `completed` candidate may suppress, verify it actually executed the leg: `gh api repos/{repo}/actions/runs/{id}/jobs` and require a non-`dedup` job with conclusion `success`. One extra API call only when a candidate exists; keeps the module pure via an injected transport hook.
2. Give the `dedup` job an `if:` mirroring the arming gate (see the runner-burn comment on the workflow) so non-arming events produce zero executed jobs — those runs then conclude `failure` (the gh-676 phantom pattern) and own nothing.

Note the unit suite cannot catch this today: the tests feed synthetic run lists where `conclusion: 'success'` is assumed to mean "the leg ran". A regression test needs the transport-level distinction from option 1, or the zero-job conclusion from option 2.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the unguarded `dedup` job allocates a runner for EVERY label write — gh-1029 no-burn regression**

The `dedup` job has no `if:`, and `on: issues: types: [assigned, labeled]` fires on every label write on every issue — including the lifecycle-label storms the legs themselves generate (`status:*`, `ai_developed`, …). gh-1029 deliberately made those events no-burn: the run's only job was skipped by the gate, zero jobs executed, no runner allocated. This PR keeps the skip but adds a real `ubuntu-latest` runner + checkout + node boot (~30–60 s of runner time) per label write, repo-wide, around the clock.

The preflight correctly avoids *API* calls for non-arming events, but the runner burn remains. Please add an `if:` to the `dedup` job mirroring the `teammate` gate (dispatch OR (assigned AND ai-teammate assignee) OR labeled with an arming label). Behaviour is unchanged for admitted events; rejected events return to true zero-burn.

Side benefit relevant to the freshness-window blocker on `isFreshlyCompleted`: with the `dedup` job skipped, those runs execute zero jobs and conclude `failure` (the gh-676 phantom pattern documented in this same file) — so they stop owning the dedup key entirely.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the wildcard leg + 10-min fresh-success window swallows genuinely sequential human actions**

`legsCompatible` wildcards an unknown leg on either side — correct for the in-flight burst (event-path titles carry no leg, and a bare assign declares none). But the same wildcard is applied to `completed` runs inside the freshness window, where the owner is an event-path run titled `teammate: issues #1040 ` (leg `''`).

Consequence: human assigns the issue at T (leg runs, completes `success` at T+4 min). At T+6 min the same human deliberately adds `agent:review` — a genuinely new request, not a burst duplicate. The probe sees the T+4 `success` run: same issue, leg wildcard-compatible, older run_number → **dropped**. The module docstring claims "a later human re-assign is never swallowed", but that only holds after the 10-minute window; any second, *different-leg* arming action within the window is swallowed.

Please confirm this is intended (the PR notes treat the 10-min bound as covering "burst event delivery + queue lag", i.e. seconds — while a human's next deliberate action often lands minutes later, within the same active session). If not intended, consider scoping the wildcard to in-flight owners only: a wildcard **in-flight** owner is almost certainly the same burst; a `completed` owner with unknown leg suppressing a KNOWN new leg is exactly the sequential-action case. At minimum, the docstring's "never swallowed" claim should be corrected.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: space-joined env lists break label/login names containing spaces**

`ISSUE_LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}` (and `ASSIGNEES` two lines below) are re-split with `.split(' ')` in the probe. GitHub label names may contain spaces (e.g. `status:in progress`), and a label/login token containing a space is silently fractured — `agent:dev` would survive, but any future arming label with a space, or an assignee login, would mismatch. Today this is latent (all five arming labels are space-free), but the parse silently degrades.

Prefer a JSON encoding: `ISSUE_LABELS: ${{ toJson(github.event.issue.labels.*.name) }}` and `JSON.parse(env.ISSUE_LABELS || '[]')` in the probe. Same for assignees.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment5.md"}

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1071
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1071
- **Title**: gh-1065 [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1065` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +1250
- **Deletions**: -26
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:30:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T22:27:38Z

## PR Description

Closes #1065
### Root Cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` and each event started its own run — one human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM `workflow_dispatch` path only; the GitHub-event path bypassed it (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs, owner hand-cancelling duplicates). The per-issue `concurrency:` group only serialized the duplicates into queued no-op burns — it never dropped them.

### Fix

- `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (new): the unit-tested pure decision, gh-1028 parity — same issue + same leg (title-parsed; unknown leg wildcards on either side, known legs must be equal), in-flight (active states, 6h stale-zombie bound) or freshly-completed `success` (10-min freshness window — burst duplicates reach the probe only after the concurrency group releases the first run) ⇒ skip. Strict run_number tie-break: only an OLDER run suppresses, so exactly one survivor per same-second burst. Fail-open on missing/garbled run data (AC3).
- `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`: new `dedup` probe job (per-status `gh api` fan-out, smAgent parity; short-circuits before any API call for `workflow_dispatch`, non-arming lifecycle labels, non-teammate assignees — gh-1029 no-burn parity; catch-all probe-error fail-open). The `teammate` call now gates on `needs: dedup.outputs.proceed == 'true'`; dropped duplicates emit a `::warning::` audit line (AC1). Dispatch-path behaviour unchanged.
- `js/unit-tests/test_teammateEventDedup.js` + `run_teammateEventDedup.json` (new), added to `run_all.json`.

### Test Coverage

- `test_teammateEventDedup.js` — 30 tests, incl. AC4 (simulated assigned+labeled burst → exactly one dispatch + one skip-audit entry; three-event gh-1061 shape), AC2 (fresh-success suppression after concurrency release; known different leg never swallowed; 6h zombie parity), AC3 (broken/missing probe data proceeds). **PASS**
- Workflow wiring guard: dedup job, `needs.dedup` gate, fail-open anchors asserted against the YAML. **PASS**
- Transport smoke: embedded probe script executed against a mocked `gh` — duplicate drop, earliest-proceeds tie-break, 5/5-status-degraded fail-open, dispatch preflight all verified.
- Full suite `run_all.json`: **4548 passed, 0 failed** (was 4548-green baseline + 30 new).

### Notes

- Freshness window is 10 min by design (documented in the module): long enough for burst event delivery + queue lag, short enough that a later human re-assign is never swallowed. Only `conclusion: success` owns the window — cancelled/failed runs leave the retry path open.
- `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (consumer-repo copy) not touched — its run titles already carry the leg; a follow-up can mirror the gate there if wanted.
- The probe adds one small job per arming event (~seconds: checkout + ≤5 API calls); lifecycle-label events short-circuit with zero API calls.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `decideEventDedup` cannot pass the `crap` quality gate (CI is red)**

The `crap` check failed on this PR (log fetch was unavailable, but I reproduced the measurement locally with the workflow's exact pinned tool, `IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d` from `.github/workflows/quality.yml:26-27`):

```text
decideEventDedup   js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 27
issueOfRunName     js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 11
legOfRunName       js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 9
isOlderRun         js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 9
```

`quality.yml` sets `CRAP_THRESHOLD: 8` and fails when *a function not in the released baseline exceeds the threshold*. All four functions are new, so none is baselined. Since CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)³ + CC, the best possible value (100% coverage) is CRAP = CC — so `decideEventDedup` scores **≥ 27** no matter how well the 30 tests cover it. The gate cannot go green without refactoring.

Please decompose `decideEventDedup` (e.g. extract the per-run suppressor predicate into a named helper — the six-condition loop body — and split the early-return verdict builders), and simplify `issueOfRunName`/`legOfRunName` (the two regex families could share one anchored-token scanner). Re-run `crap4js --threshold 8 js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` to confirm before pushing.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: runs that never executed the teammate leg own the freshness window — the first GENUINE trigger is silently swallowed**

`isFreshlyCompleted` (and the transport around it) treats any `status: completed` + `conclusion: success` run of this workflow as an owner of the issue+leg key. But run-level success no longer implies the leg ran, because the new `dedup` job **always executes and always succeeds** (its catch-all is fail-open by design):

- A non-arming lifecycle label write (`status:*`, `ai_developed`, … — which the legs themselves write constantly, see the gh-1029 comment in the workflow) creates a run whose `teammate` job is skipped by the gate. The `dedup` job succeeds → **the run concludes `success`**, titled `teammate: issues #1040 ` (same issue anchor, leg `''` → wildcard-compatible).
- Now a human assigns the issue to `ai-teammate (or adds `agent:review`) within 10 minutes of that label write. The probe finds this fresh `success` run, older run_number → `duplicate` → **the first and only real trigger is dropped**, with nothing but a `::warning::` line inside a run that GitHub shows as green.

This breaks AC1 in the dangerous direction (zero runs instead of one), and it contradicts AC3's spirit — a dedup check silently swallowing the only trigger. During active work on an issue (labels being written by legs), event-path triggers are effectively suppressed for 10 minutes after ANY run of this workflow, successful or not.

Suggested directions (either or both):
1. Before a `completed` candidate may suppress, verify it actually executed the leg: `gh api repos/{repo}/actions/runs/{id}/jobs` and require a non-`dedup` job with conclusion `success`. One extra API call only when a candidate exists; keeps the module pure via an injected transport hook.
2. Give the `dedup` job an `if:` mirroring the arming gate (see the runner-burn comment on the workflow) so non-arming events produce zero executed jobs — those runs then conclude `failure` (the gh-676 phantom pattern) and own nothing.

Note the unit suite cannot catch this today: the tests feed synthetic run lists where `conclusion: 'success'` is assumed to mean "the leg ran". A regression test needs the transport-level distinction from option 1, or the zero-job conclusion from option 2.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the unguarded `dedup` job allocates a runner for EVERY label write — gh-1029 no-burn regression**

The `dedup` job has no `if:`, and `on: issues: types: [assigned, labeled]` fires on every label write on every issue — including the lifecycle-label storms the legs themselves generate (`status:*`, `ai_developed`, …). gh-1029 deliberately made those events no-burn: the run's only job was skipped by the gate, zero jobs executed, no runner allocated. This PR keeps the skip but adds a real `ubuntu-latest` runner + checkout + node boot (~30–60 s of runner time) per label write, repo-wide, around the clock.

The preflight correctly avoids *API* calls for non-arming events, but the runner burn remains. Please add an `if:` to the `dedup` job mirroring the `teammate` gate (dispatch OR (assigned AND ai-teammate assignee) OR labeled with an arming label). Behaviour is unchanged for admitted events; rejected events return to true zero-burn.

Side benefit relevant to the freshness-window blocker on `isFreshlyCompleted`: with the `dedup` job skipped, those runs execute zero jobs and conclude `failure` (the gh-676 phantom pattern documented in this same file) — so they stop owning the dedup key entirely.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the wildcard leg + 10-min fresh-success window swallows genuinely sequential human actions**

`legsCompatible` wildcards an unknown leg on either side — correct for the in-flight burst (event-path titles carry no leg, and a bare assign declares none). But the same wildcard is applied to `completed` runs inside the freshness window, where the owner is an event-path run titled `teammate: issues #1040 ` (leg `''`).

Consequence: human assigns the issue at T (leg runs, completes `success` at T+4 min). At T+6 min the same human deliberately adds `agent:review` — a genuinely new request, not a burst duplicate. The probe sees the T+4 `success` run: same issue, leg wildcard-compatible, older run_number → **dropped**. The module docstring claims "a later human re-assign is never swallowed", but that only holds after the 10-minute window; any second, *different-leg* arming action within the window is swallowed.

Please confirm this is intended (the PR notes treat the 10-min bound as covering "burst event delivery + queue lag", i.e. seconds — while a human's next deliberate action often lands minutes later, within the same active session). If not intended, consider scoping the wildcard to in-flight owners only: a wildcard **in-flight** owner is almost certainly the same burst; a `completed` owner with unknown leg suppressing a KNOWN new leg is exactly the sequential-action case. At minimum, the docstring's "never swallowed" claim should be corrected.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: space-joined env lists break label/login names containing spaces**

`ISSUE_LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}` (and `ASSIGNEES` two lines below) are re-split with `.split(' ')` in the probe. GitHub label names may contain spaces (e.g. `status:in progress`), and a label/login token containing a space is silently fractured — `agent:dev` would survive, but any future arming label with a space, or an assignee login, would mismatch. Today this is latent (all five arming labels are space-free), but the parse silently degrades.

Prefer a JSON encoding: `ISSUE_LABELS: ${{ toJson(github.event.issue.labels.*.name) }}` and `JSON.parse(env.ISSUE_LABELS || '[]')` in the probe. Same for assignees.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: track the template mirror as a follow-up ticket**

The PR notes (correctly) leave `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` untouched — its consumer-repo copies keep the un-deduped event path, so every consumer repo still burns duplicate teammate runs on assign-while-labels-change, and the template's run titles already carry the leg so the pure module would slot in directly. Please file a linked follow-up ticket so this deferred scope doesn't evaporate; a one-line mention in the module header (`DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_FILE` consumers) would also help the next reade…

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

# gh-1065: the title carries the LEG for every path — the dispatch input
# leg directly, and for event-path runs the strongest arming label on the
# issue (rework > review > pr_approved → review > dev). legOfRunName
# (js/common/teammateEventDedup.js) parses the trailing token, so a
# COMPLETED owner stays title-precise: the strict completed-owner leg rule
# (a leg-less completed run never swallows a KNOWN new leg) can only work
# when real leg runs carry their leg in the title.
run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && 'rework') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && 'review') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'pr_approved') && 'review') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:dev') && 'dev') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:develop') && 'dev') || github.event.label.name }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # gh-1065 (live 2026-10-18, issues #1040–#1043 / #1061): one human action
  # (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits MULTIPLE issues events and
  # each event started its own run — two per issue, three on #1061, the
  # owner hand-cancelling duplicates. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM
  # dispatch path only; this job is the missing event-path gate. It probes
  # the repo's ai-teammate.yml runs (per-status gh api fan-out, smAgent
  # parity) and lets the `teammate` call fire only when no OLDER run for
  # the same issue + leg is in flight or freshly completed. Probe errors
  # FAIL OPEN (AC3): a broken check writes proceed=true so the only trigger
  # of a burst is never silently swallowed. The decision itself is the
  # unit-tested pure module js/common/teammateEventDedup.js (AC4) — this
  # step is transport only. The probe short-circuits BEFORE any API call
  # for workflow_dispatch (SM-side gh-1028 governs it), non-arming
  # lifecycle labels and non-teammate assignees.
  dedup:
    name: Event-path dedup probe (gh-1065)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1065 rework (review thread — gh-1029 zero-burn parity): this gate
    # MIRRORS the teammate call gate below. `on:` fires on EVERY label
    # write repo-wide, and an unguarded dedup job would allocate a runner
    # (checkout + node boot) per lifecycle-label storm — the exact burn
    # gh-1029 eliminated. Rejected events now execute ZERO jobs: the run
    # concludes failure (the gh-676 phantom pattern) and — because only
    # conclusion 'success' owns the freshness window — can never suppress
    # a trigger for an issue whose leg never ran.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    outputs:
      proceed: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.proceed }}
      audit: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.audit }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - id: probe
        name: Decide whether this event duplicates an in-flight teammate run
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          LABEL_NAME: ${{ github.event.label.name }}
          ISSUE_LABELS: ${{ toJson(github.event.issue.labels.*.name) }}
          ISSUE: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ toJson(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login) }}
          SELF_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          SELF_RUN_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          WORKFLOW_FILE: ai-teammate.yml
          # GITHUB_OUTPUT is provided by the runner — do NOT set it here.
        run: |
          node <<'DEDUP_PROBE_EOF'
          const { execFileSync } = require('child_process');
          const fs = require('fs');
          const dedup = require('./js/common/teammateEventDedup.js');

          const env = process.env;
          // gh-1065 rework (review thread): label/login names may contain
          // spaces — the lists ride as JSON. Fallback: the legacy
          // space-joined shape still parses (defense in depth).

No — burst means assign+label change. Consider: human assigns (no labels on issue) → run 500 proceeds, executes (factory derives leg somehow — maybe nothing to do), completes success at T+4 with leg-less title. At T+6 min, same human assigns AGAIN (deliberate retry/re-arm — "a second bare assign inside the window is burst noise" per the new doc). The module treats the second bare assign as burst noise and DROPS it. Is that right? A deliberate re-assign within 10 min is plausibly a genuine new request... but this is the documented tradeoff, accepted. Fine.

**Issue B — the both-unknown completed rule vs the AC2 burst**: assign-while-labels-change on an issue that already had NO arming labels... wait, assign-while-labels-change means labels ARE being changed. If the label change includes adding 'bug' (non-arming) and removing... the arming-label-derived title leg depends on the issue's CURRENT arming labels. If the human's action adds `agent:dev`: run 500 (assigned) title carries 'dev'; run 501 (labeled agent:dev) title carries 'dev'; completed strict: both known equal → 501 drops ✓.

If the human's action REMOVES `agent:dev` (unlabels) — no event (trigger is assigned+labeled only... 'unlabeled' not in types). OK.

If the human assigns while a teammate-added lifecycle label changes: run 500 assigned with issue having only lifecycle labels → title leg-less. Run 501 labeled status:whatever → **the dedup job's if: REJECTS it** (non-arming) → run 501 zero jobs → conclusion failure → owns nothing ✓. Good — this is the thread-2/3 fix working together.

**Issue C — title leg derivation race in the burst**: run 500 (assigned) created BEFORE the agent:dev label lands (assign event processed first, label added 200ms later): run 500's title = leg-less (no arming label at run creation). Run 501 (labeled agent:dev): title carries 'dev' (label present by then). Sequence: run 500 proceeds (first), executes dev leg, completes success, leg-less title. Run 501 probes: completed owner leg=' vs event leg='dev' → completedLegsCompatible('dev',') = false → **run 501 PROCEDS** → duplicate dev leg runs twice (serialized by concurrency, but both execute). This re-opens AC1/AC2 for the assign-then-label ordering! The rework's own note says: "Without it [run-name leg carry], scoping the wildcard would have re-opened the AC2 hole: the first burst run's title would be leg-less when the labeled duplicate's probe runs after completion" — they fixed the case where the label is already present at run-500 creation. But the ORDER MATTERS: if the `assigned` event run is created before the label write is visible, its title is leg-less and the labeled duplicate (known leg) proceeds.

How likely is that ordering? GitHub delivers events within ~seconds; run-name is evaluated at run creation from the issue's label list at that moment. The `labeled` event implies the label was added — the issue's labels at that moment include it. For run 500 (created from the assigned event), if GitHub processes assigned first (same-second burst), the label may NOT yet be on the issue → leg-less title. Then the labeled duplicate proceeds. This is exactly the AC4 scenario with the events in the other order. Hmm — but wait: in the AC4 scenario, the FIRST event's run is the one that executes; the second event's run probes AFTER the first completes (concurrency). So the duplicate executes the leg a second time ~minutes later. Violates AC1 (exactly ONE run) — the failure mode is duplicate work (the original bug), not suppression. It's a partial reopen: same-leg burst where the first run's title is leg-less AND the second event is labeled-with-known-leg.

Mitigating factors: with a bare assign (no labels), title leg-less; but the burst observed live (#1040–#1043) was "assign-while-labels-change" — labels changed simultaneously. If the human adds agent:dev AND assigns in one action, whichever event GitHub creates first... the labeled event's run sees the label; the assigned event's run may or may not. Probability ~50% per issue. So this fix reduces duplicates but doesn't eliminate them in this ordering. Is this worth flaging? It's a real residual hole in AC1. The previous review's in-flight wildcard covered it; the completed strict rule re-opens it when the owner completed before the probe. Given the burst's earliest run is what executes, and its title may be leg-less... yes — IMPORTANT finding (correctness gap, re-opens part of AC1). Actually could it be BLOCKING? AC1: "Assigning an issue (with or without a simultaneous label event) yields exactly ONE teammate run per issue per leg". With ~50% ordering, two dev legs run. But it's a re-review; the blocker thread-2 was about suppression (worse). This one causes duplicate burns — the very thing the ticket targets. I rate it IMPORTANT-to-BLOCKING... Let me think about whether there's a cheap fix: the labeled duplicate's probe could also treat a completed leg-less owner as compatible when the event is labeled and the label is now on the issue (i.e., the owner run's title resolution is racy) — e.g., completed rule: both-unknown OR both-known-equal OR (event leg known AND owner completed BEFORE the label landed?) — unknowable. Simpler fix: make `assigned`-event runs not claim the title leg... no.

Actually alternative robust fix: keep strict completed rule, but the labeled event leg derivation could ALSO consider `env.LABEL_NAME` already does. The hole is owner-side (title leg-less). Given the run-name is computed once at creation, you can't fix retroactively. But note: run 501's title carries 'dev'. If instead the module treated "completed owner with unknown leg + same issue + owner is OLDER" as compatible ONLY when the event is `assigned` (both-unknown case handles bare assigns)... that's the current behavior. The labeled-known-leg vs leg-less completed owner proceeds. Hmm.

Practical assessment: this residual duplicates at most ONE extra leg run per burst in the unfavorable ordering, serialized behind the first — exactly the pre-fix behavior for that ordering, not a regression vs main. But the PR claims AC1 fixed. I'll raise as IMPORTANT (question + suggested mitigation: e.g., for a completed leg-less owner, also compare the owner's created_at against... nothing available. Or: the run-name for the assigned event could prefer... nothing. Honestly the cleanest mitigation is the jobs-API verification to check whether the owner run actually executed the same leg — but titles don't record inputs... The factory reusable workflow receives `leg: ''` for event paths and derives internally — not visible. So a full fix is hard; flag as a known residual with a suggested cheap dampener: also suppress when the completed owner is leg-less AND the event is `labeled` with known leg AND the owner's title was created within the same burst window... that's basically re-wildcarding. State it as an open tradeoff question — IMPORTANT).

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `decideEventDedup` cannot pass the `crap` quality gate (CI is red)**

The `crap` check failed on this PR (log fetch was unavailable, but I reproduced the measurement locally with the workflow's exact pinned tool, `IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d` from `.github/workflows/quality.yml:26-27`):

```text
decideEventDedup   js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 27
issueOfRunName     js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 11
legOfRunName       js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 9
isOlderRun         js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 9
```

`quality.yml` sets `CRAP_THRESHOLD: 8` and fails when *a function not in the released baseline exceeds the threshold*. All four functions are new, so none is baselined. Since CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)³ + CC, the best possible value (100% coverage) is CRAP = CC — so `decideEventDedup` scores **≥ 27** no matter how well the 30 tests cover it. The gate cannot go green without refactoring.

Please decompose `decideEventDedup` (e.g. extract the per-run suppressor predicate into a named helper — the six-condition loop body — and split the early-return verdict builders), and simplify `issueOfRunName`/`legOfRunName` (the two regex families could share one anchored-token scanner). Re-run `crap4js --threshold 8 js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` to confirm before pushing.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: runs that never executed the teammate leg own the freshness window — the first GENUINE trigger is silently swallowed**

`isFreshlyCompleted` (and the transport around it) treats any `status: completed` + `conclusion: success` run of this workflow as an owner of the issue+leg key. But run-level success no longer implies the leg ran, because the new `dedup` job **always executes and always succeeds** (its catch-all is fail-open by design):

- A non-arming lifecycle label write (`status:*`, `ai_developed`, … — which the legs themselves write constantly, see the gh-1029 comment in the workflow) creates a run whose `teammate` job is skipped by the gate. The `dedup` job succeeds → **the run concludes `success`**, titled `teammate: issues #1040 ` (same issue anchor, leg `''` → wildcard-compatible).
- Now a human assigns the issue to `ai-teammate (or adds `agent:review`) within 10 minutes of that label write. The probe finds this fresh `success` run, older run_number → `duplicate` → **the first and only real trigger is dropped**, with nothing but a `::warning::` line inside a run that GitHub shows as green.

This breaks AC1 in the dangerous direction (zero runs instead of one), and it contradicts AC3's spirit — a dedup check silently swallowing the only trigger. During active work on an issue (labels being written by legs), event-path triggers are effectively suppressed for 10 minutes after ANY run of this workflow, successful or not.

Suggested directions (either or both):
1. Before a `completed` candidate may suppress, verify it actually executed the leg: `gh api repos/{repo}/actions/runs/{id}/jobs` and require a non-`dedup` job with conclusion `success`. One extra API call only when a candidate exists; keeps the module pure via an injected transport hook.
2. Give the `dedup` job an `if:` mirroring the arming gate (see the runner-burn comment on the workflow) so non-arming events produce zero executed jobs — those runs then conclude `failure` (the gh-676 phantom pattern) and own nothing.

Note the unit suite cannot catch this today: the tests feed synthetic run lists where `conclusion: 'success'` is assumed to mean "the leg ran". A regression test needs the transport-level distinction from option 1, or the zero-job conclusion from option 2.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the unguarded `dedup` job allocates a runner for EVERY label write — gh-1029 no-burn regression**

The `dedup` job has no `if:`, and `on: issues: types: [assigned, labeled]` fires on every label write on every issue — including the lifecycle-label storms the legs themselves generate (`status:*`, `ai_developed`, …). gh-1029 deliberately made those events no-burn: the run's only job was skipped by the gate, zero jobs executed, no runner allocated. This PR keeps the skip but adds a real `ubuntu-latest` runner + checkout + node boot (~30–60 s of runner time) per label write, repo-wide, around the clock.

The preflight correctly avoids *API* calls for non-arming events, but the runner burn remains. Please add an `if:` to the `dedup` job mirroring the `teammate` gate (dispatch OR (assigned AND ai-teammate assignee) OR labeled with an arming label). Behaviour is unchanged for admitted events; rejected events return to true zero-burn.

Side benefit relevant to the freshness-window blocker on `isFreshlyCompleted`: with the `dedup` job skipped, those runs execute zero jobs and conclude `failure` (the gh-676 phantom pattern documented in this same file) — so they stop owning the dedup key entirely.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the wildcard leg + 10-min fresh-success window swallows genuinely sequential human actions**

`legsCompatible` wildcards an unknown leg on either side — correct for the in-flight burst (event-path titles carry no leg, and a bare assign declares none). But the same wildcard is applied to `completed` runs inside the freshness window, where the owner is an event-path run titled `teammate: issues #1040 ` (leg `''`).

Consequence: human assigns the issue at T (leg runs, completes `success` at T+4 min). At T+6 min the same human deliberately adds `agent:review` — a genuinely new request, not a burst duplicate. The probe sees the T+4 `success` run: same issue, leg wildcard-compatible, older run_number → **dropped**. The module docstring claims "a later human re-assign is never swallowed", but that only holds after the 10-minute window; any second, *different-leg* arming action within the window is swallowed.

Please confirm this is intended (the PR notes treat the 10-min bound as covering "burst event delivery + queue lag", i.e. seconds — while a human's next deliberate action often lands minutes later, within the same active session). If not intended, consider scoping the wildcard to in-flight owners only: a wildcard **in-flight** owner is almost certainly the same burst; a `completed` owner with unknown leg suppressing a KNOWN new leg is exactly the sequential-action case. At minimum, the docstring's "never swallowed" claim should be corrected.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: space-joined env lists break label/login names containing spaces**

`ISSUE_LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}` (and `ASSIGNEES` two lines below) are re-split with `.split(' ')` in the probe. GitHub label names may contain spaces (e.g. `status:in progress`), and a label/login token containing a space is silently fractured — `agent:dev` would survive, but any future arming label with a space, or an assignee login, would mismatch. Today this is latent (all five arming labels are space-free), but the parse silently degrades.

Prefer a JSON encoding: `ISSUE_LABELS: ${{ toJson(github.event.issue.labels.*.name) }}` and `JSON.parse(env.ISSUE_LABELS || '[]')` in the probe. Same for assignees.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment5.md"}

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8.
